lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Well, well, well...
lines.script: [easy] Well, well, well...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look who flew three thousand miles to see me.
lines.script: [smooth, amused] Look who flew three thousand miles to see me.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: How many SkyMiles is that now?
lines.script: [skeptical] How many SkyMiles is that now?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe! What are you saving them for?
lines.script: [amused annoyed] Babe. What are you saving them for?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You said that at three hundred thousand.
lines.script: [slightly skeptical] You said that at three hundred thousand.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Zero miles. Babe. That's the most romantic thing a Delta person can say.
lines.script: [quietly touched] Zero miles. Babe. [dry] That's the most romantic thing a Delta person can say.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My call time got pushed to Thursday. The lead actor lost a shoe. I already found it. So I'm all yours.
lines.script: [easy, wry] My call time got pushed to Thursday. [deadpan, casual] The lead actor lost a shoe. I already found it. [warm, soft] So I'm all yours.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The mud took Deedee's crisp? Is the mud okay?
lines.script: [genuinely concerned] The mud took Deedee's crisp? [sincere, softly concerned] Is the mud okay?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: A talking fish! What did he say?
lines.script: [quietly pleased] A talking fish. [quietly pleased, curious] What did he say?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Mud in the kitchen and a talking fish. Babe, something fishy is going on.
lines.script: [tallying, nonchalant] Mud in the kitchen and a talking fish. [punchline] Babe, something fishy is going on.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He hasn't been alone. Come on, I'll show you.
lines.script: [knowing, teasing] He hasn't been alone. [inviting] Come on, I'll show you.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It's been like that since this morning. I held my soda up to it. It's the exact same color.
lines.script: [resigned, nonchalant] It's been like that since this morning. [investigating] I held my soda up to it. [pleasantly surprised] It's the exact same color.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I don't know what it is, babe. But it's pretty grape.
lines.script: [nonchalant] I don't know what it is, babe. [punchline] But it's pretty grape.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Olivia dropped her off this morning. Family trip to the desert. No dogs at the hotel.
lines.script: [easy, warm] Olivia dropped her off this morning. [easy, matter-of-fact] Family trip to the desert. [dry] No dogs at the hotel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's been sitting on your porch since eight. I tried to take her to the loft. She refused.
lines.script: [easy, amused] She's been sitting on your porch since eight. [dry, rueful] I tried to take her to the loft. [deadpan] She refused.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: So I stayed here with her. I was coming over anyway. I've been feeding Bready Mercury every day.
lines.script: [casual] So I stayed here with her. [downplaying] I was coming over anyway. [quietly proud] I've been feeding Bready Mercury every day.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Fifty and fifty. I used your little scale.
lines.script: [patient, reassuring] Fifty and fifty. [amused] I used your little scale.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He got so big he was climbing out of the jar. So I baked a loaf with him.
lines.script: [amused] He got so big he was climbing out of the jar. [nonchalant] So I baked a loaf with him.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I shaped it on my pottery wheel.
lines.script: [nonchalant, proud] I shaped it on my pottery wheel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I make bowls all day, babe. So I made you a bread bowl.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I make bowls all day, babe. [punchline] So I made you a bread bowl.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I sing to him while I stir. He's Bready Mercury. He needs his music.
lines.script: [nonchalant] I sing to him while I stir. [stating the obvious] He's Bready Mercury. [dead serious] He needs his music.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: "Another One Bites the Crust."
lines.script: [deadpan] "Another One Bites the... [punchline] crust."

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. That's so good. I'm singing that one tomorrow.
lines.script: [quietly impressed] Babe. [admiring] That's so good. [nonchalant] I'm singing that one tomorrow.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Look outside. Is the street... purple?
lines.script: [easy, puzzled] Babe. Look outside. [slow, uneasy] Is the street... purple?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He always finishes that story. I've heard it nine times. It ends with gumbo.
lines.script: [fond] He always finishes that story. [nonchalant] I've heard it nine times. [softly concerned] It ends with gumbo.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. That cloud has a face. And it just talked to us.
lines.script: [low-key concerned, hushed] Babe. That cloud has a face. [quiet quiet quiet disbelief] And it just talked to us.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You did tell me. It's a lot scarier in person.
lines.script: [admitting] You did tell me. [low-key concerned] It's a lot scarier in person.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Scarier than movie night. Remember? You threw the whole popcorn bowl.
lines.script: [low-key, amused] Scarier than movie night. [dry, teasing] Remember? You threw the whole popcorn bowl.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And it rained popcorn on the whole room. Let's do that to these clouds.
lines.script: [amused, remembering] And it rained popcorn on the whole room. [scheming] Let's do that to these clouds.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You don't need popcorn. You just need to be that scared.
lines.script: [reassuring] You don't need popcorn. [coaching] You just need to be that scared.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Everybody breathe. Through the nose. Not the smog.
lines.script: [calm, steadying] Okay. Okay. Everybody breathe. [dry, easy] Through the nose. Not the smog.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The smog monsters are gone, but Mr. Washington is still in a daze. Look at him.
lines.script: [low, softly concerned] The smog monsters are gone, but Mr. [quiet, uneasy] Washington is still in a daze. Look at him.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: If the smog did this to him, what about everybody on the boulevard?
lines.script: [softly concerned, realizing] If the smog did this to him, what about everybody on the boulevard?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Miss Odette, it's me! Can I get a bowl of gumbo?
lines.script: [quietly pleased, hopeful] Miss Odette, it's me. [charming] Can I get a bowl of gumbo?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, this is bad. Every time I walk in here she yells "Sit down, you're too skinny!" before the door even closes.
lines.script: [softly concerned] Babe, this is bad. [explaining] Every time I walk in here she yells [imitating her, bossy] "Sit down, you're too skinny." [softly concerned] before the door even closes.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, the pupusas are burning!
lines.script: [low-key concerned] Babe, the pupusas are burning.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She smacks you with that towel if you even look at the griddle.
lines.script: [whispering, awed] She smacks you with that towel if you even look at the griddle.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Nara is right. That's not kitchen smoke. It's the same purple smog, and it's blowing down from the hills.
lines.script: [low, alert] Nara is right. [tense, wry] That's not kitchen smoke. It's the same purple smog, and it's blowing down from the hills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Look north. It's all coming down off the hills.
lines.script: [low, calm] Babe. Look north. [uneasy, hushed] It's all coming down off the hills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It's coming from the Observatory. The pipes on its side are pumping out smog like a smoke machine on a bad set.
lines.script: [dry, grim] It's coming from the Observatory. [dry, flat] The pipes on its side are pumping out smog like a smoke machine on a bad set.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I take the Metro. You have nothing on me.
lines.script: [smooth, smug] I take the Metro. [dry, unbothered] You have nothing on me.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up, everybody. Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.
lines.script: [easy, calm] Up, everybody. [wry, warm] Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We do have snacks, though. I've got half a bag of gummy worms.
lines.script: [helpful, nonchalant] We do have snacks, though. [offering] I've got half a bag of gummy worms.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Quick wardrobe adjustment, quick heal, and a quick kiss for the road. Ready, babe?
lines.script: [easy, flirty] Quick wardrobe adjustment, quick heal, and a quick kiss for the road. [teasing, soft] Ready, babe?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, look at that tree. It's grey. The leaves, the trunk, even the dirt. It looks like an old black and white movie.
lines.script: [uneasy] Babe, look at that tree. [quiet quiet quiet disbelief] It's grey. [listing, unsettled] The leaves, the trunk, even the dirt. [awed] It looks like an old black and white movie.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: On Long Island? Babe, that's three thousand miles away.
lines.script: [low-key concerned] On Long Island? [nonchalant] Babe, that's three thousand miles away.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It's not glass, and it's not glaze. I work with this kind of stuff all day and I have no idea what it is.
lines.script: [investigating] It's not glass, and it's not glaze. [stumped] I work with this kind of stuff all day and I have no idea what it is.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: There's a little round hole in the side, like somebody took a bite out of it.
lines.script: [investigating] There's a little round hole in the side, [uneasy] like somebody took a bite out of it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Can I try anyway?
lines.script: [undeterred, nonchalant] Can I try anyway?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Wow. Your turn.
lines.script: [quietly impressed] Okay. Wow. [conceding] Your turn.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Who leaves the same bulb at a pond in New York and on a hill in Los Angeles?
lines.script: [puzzling it out] Who leaves the same bulb at a pond in New York... [uneasy] and on a hill in Los Angeles?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Me neither. And I like almost everything.
lines.script: [agreeing, shaken] Me neither. [punchline, deadpan] And I like almost everything.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The ground is humming. That's never a good sign. I've seen this movie forty-seven times.
lines.script: [low, uneasy] The ground is humming. That's never a good sign. [dry, ominous] I've seen this movie forty-seven times.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. I take naps on that hill.
lines.script: [low-key concerned, hushed] Babe. [confessing] I take naps on that hill.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'm so sorry, sir!
lines.script: [low-key concerned, apologizing] I'm so sorry, sir.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He'd know. He has four hundred and twelve thousand miles.
lines.script: [dry, vouching for him] He'd know. [dry, fond] He has four hundred and twelve thousand miles.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Well, well, well... looks like we're in a bit of a shaky situation.
lines.script: [playful, smooth] Well, well, well... [dry, punny] looks like we're in a bit of a shaky situation.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Cut. Reset. Back to one, everybody.
lines.script: [calm] Cut. Reset. [calm, easy] Back to one, everybody.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, heal right after the Aftershock. When it clogs up, hit it with water or sparkle. Or one of our Tombos.
lines.script: [easy, coaching] Babe, heal right after the Aftershock. [calm, practical] When it clogs up, hit it with water or sparkle. [wry, upbeat] Or one of our Tombos.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'm sorry I kept falling asleep on you. I didn't know you were a person.
lines.script: [apologizing, sincere] I'm sorry I kept falling asleep on you. [sheepish] I didn't know you were a person.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The one the fish gave her?
lines.script: [checking] The one the fish gave her?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Nara thinks it's a very small frisbee.
lines.script: [amused, observing] Nara thinks it's a very small frisbee.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look. The sky is blue again. Los Angeles blue. Slightly brown, but blue.
lines.script: [relieved, easy] Look. The sky is blue again. Los Angeles blue. [deadpan, fond] Slightly brown, but blue.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Two flashes, two orange blocks and two gold coins. Babe, I don't love that. Let's go check on Mr. Washington.
lines.script: [tallying, slowly] Two flashes, two orange blocks and two gold coins. [understating, uneasy] Babe, I don't love that. [deciding] Let's go check on Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's ten times now. It gets better every time.
lines.script: [fond, amused] That's ten times now. [sincere] It gets better every time.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Yes, ma'am!
lines.script: [quietly pleased, obedient] yes, ma'am.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Gumbo. Go get the bread bowl!
lines.script: [quietly pleased, realizing] Babe. Gumbo. [calm] Go get the bread bowl.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's not a hole. That's where the gumbo goes in.
lines.script: [reassuring] That's not a hole. [punchline] That's where the gumbo goes in.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: With two thousand four hundred and seventy-five miles in between.
lines.script: [tender, wistful] With two thousand four hundred and seventy-five miles in between.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey, you. Did you eat? I made a bowl. I also made a bowl. Pottery joke.
lines.script: [warm, easy] Hey, you. Did you eat? I made a bowl. [sly, amused] I also made a bowl. [dry, pleased] Pottery joke.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Welcome to the loft. Kiln by one window, wheel by the other, garment bags everywhere else. Spring Street, baby.
lines.script: [relaxed, proud] Welcome to the loft. Kiln by one window, wheel by the other, garment bags everywhere else. [warm, fond] Spring Street, baby.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Take my jacket. It gets cold up in Griffith Park at night, and a cold Tom is a no-go.
lines.script: [tender, easy] Take my jacket. It gets cold up in Griffith Park at night, [soft, teasing] and a cold Tom is a no-go.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Took the longboard down Spring Street this morning. Smooth. There's a crack by Fourth Street I've named.
lines.script: [easy, content] Took the longboard down Spring Street this morning. Smooth. [dry, amused] There's a crack by Fourth Street I've named.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Threw six mugs this morning. The glaze came out of the kiln like sea glass. Come look before you claim one.
lines.script: [pleased, quietly pleased] Threw six mugs this morning. The glaze came out of the kiln like sea glass. [warm, inviting] Come look before you claim one.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Go on, I'll be right here. I'm pot-sitive about it.
lines.script: [easy, smooth] Go on, I'll be right here. [smug, amused] I'm pot-sitive about it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Horror movie tonight. You pick. You always pick the scary one and then hold my arm the whole time.
lines.script: [amused, fond] Horror movie tonight. You pick. [dry, teasing] You always pick the scary one and then hold my arm the whole time.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Watered your plants on 2nd Ave. The fern asked about you. I said you're fine.
lines.script: [easy, light] Watered your plants on 2nd Ave. [dry, amused] The fern asked about you. [soft, reassuring] I said you're fine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Rode the train to the clay studio. Forty minutes. Best forty minutes of my day. Met a man who knows every line.
lines.script: [content, easy] Rode the train to the clay studio. Forty minutes. [warm, glowing] Best forty minutes of my day. [quietly pleased] Met a man who knows every line.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The slime? It just needs someone to mold it. I have more of these. You know I do.
lines.script: [warm, low] The slime? It just needs someone to mold it. [sly, amused] I have more of these. [smooth, fond] You know I do.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Long day on set. Eleven costume changes. One actor lost a shoe. I found it. I always find it.
lines.script: [tired, wry] Long day on set. Eleven costume changes. One actor lost a shoe. [quietly proud] I found it. [smooth, easy] I always find it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Be careful out there. I like you un-cracked.
lines.script: [tender, soft] Be careful out there. [warm, teasing] I like you un-cracked.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I flew six hours for that pun?
lines.script: [dry, mock-exhausted] I flew SIX hours... [deadpan] for that pun?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Let's go home to Jefferson Park. Bready Mercury has been alone all week.
lines.script: [warm, eager] Let's go home to Jefferson Park. [fretting, doting] Bready Mercury has been alone ALL week.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "Bohemian Rye-psody!"
lines.script: [delighted, singing it out] "Bohemian... [proud of the pun] RYE-psody!"

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I couldn't pull the one at the pond out either. ...Maybe it's easier in California.
lines.script: [admitting, sheepish] I couldn't pull the one at the pond out either. [hopeful, reasoning] ...Maybe it's easier in California.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: If everybody is stuck, nobody can leave. No moving trucks. No airports. No goodbyes.
lines.script: [deep, slow, stubborn] If everybody is stuck, nobody can leave. [listing, grumbling] No moving trucks. No airports. [lonely, low] No goodbyes.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: RUMBLE. There was a big flash up here this morning, and it woke me up.
lines.script: [deep, slow, long drawn-out rumble] Rrrrrummmmmmmble... [groggy, grumpy] There was a big flash up here this morning, and it woke me up.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Rumble. You asked how I was doing. Nobody has asked in a million years.
lines.script: [deep, soft, long drawn-out rumble] Rrrummmmble... [stunned, small] You asked how I was doing. [wondering] Nobody has asked in a million years.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Rumble. Fine. The pipes are clear. I'm going back under the hill to think about my choices.
lines.script: [deep, sulky, long drawn-out rumble] Rrrummmmble... [sulky] Fine. The pipes are clear. [muttering, sheepish] I'm going back under the hill to think about my choices.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody says goodbye. Then they come back. That's what planes are for.
lines.script: [firm, heartfelt, leaning in] Everybody says goodbye. [warm, with feeling] Then they COME BACK. [proud, a little smile] That's what planes are FOR.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Things have to move.
lines.script: [gentle but firm, emphatic] Things HAVE to move.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft.
lines.script: [eager, a little giddy] TNB said he'd be home. [brisk, excited] Spring Street loft.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. So polite!
lines.script: [proud, counting it off] Sit, paw, treat. [impressed] She knows the WHOLE routine. [gushing] So polite!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello, Bready Mercury. Did you miss me? You missed me.
lines.script: [baby talk, cooing] Hello, Bready Mercury. [teasing, sing-song] Did you miss me? [delighted, certain] You MISSED me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. Look at those bubbles.
lines.script: [precise, focused] Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. [concentrating] Stir. [thrilled, proud parent] Look at those BUBBLES.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Washington! Is everything okay?
lines.script: [calling out, worried] Mr. Washington! [anxious, gentle] Is everything okay?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me, smog. That was UNCALLED for.
lines.script: [coughing, offended] Excuse me, smog. [scandalized, outraged] That was UNCALLED for.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then that's where we're going. Nara, stay close.
lines.script: [determined, steely] Then that's where we're going. [protective, tender] Nara, stay close.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Ready. Kiss accepted. The Observatory is up at the top left. Follow the purple.
lines.script: [smitten, dry] Ready. Kiss accepted. [snapping into leader mode] The Observatory is up at the top left. [determined] Follow the purple.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Keep the old windows, though.
lines.script: [dry, conspiratorial, smiling] Keep the old windows, though.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I contest that ticket, and I'm granting my own appeal. Let's keep going.
lines.script: [pompous, mock-official] I contest that ticket, [smug, triumphant] and I'm granting my own appeal. [brisk] Let's keep going.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. One down. Let's check on Doña Carmen next door.
lines.script: [relieved, exhaling] Okay. One down. [determined] Let's check on Doña Carmen next door.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. One down. Let's check on Miss Odette next door.
lines.script: [relieved, exhaling] Okay. One down. [determined] Let's check on Miss Odette next door.

lines.speaker: Boomie
lines.text: TOM! Get over here. Hug. Mmm-hmm. There it is.
lines.script: [big, booming, overjoyed to see him] Tom! [warm, insisting] Get over here. [melting, satisfied] Hug. Mmm-hmm. There it is.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Tom. Back in 1979, this whole block...
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Tom. [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone, drifting off] Back in 1979, this whole block...

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Back in 1979, this whole block...
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone, drifting off] Back in 1979, this whole block...

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Such a nice afternoon. It should always be this afternoon.
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Such a nice afternoon. [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] It should always be this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Such a nice afternoon. It should always be this afternoon. Nobody needs to get any older.
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Such a nice afternoon. It should always be this afternoon. [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Nobody needs to get any older.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Nobody needs to go anywhere. Nobody needs to get any older.
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Nobody needs to go anywhere. [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Nobody needs to get any older.

lines.speaker: Miss Odette
lines.text: Stirring. Stirring. The gumbo never has to be done, baby. Isn’t that nice?
lines.script: [light Louisiana Creole accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Stirring. ...Stirring. [light Louisiana Creole accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] The gumbo never has to be done, baby. Isn't that nice?

lines.speaker: Miss Odette
lines.text: Stirring. Stirring.
lines.script: [light Louisiana Creole accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Stirring. ...Stirring.

lines.speaker: Miss Odette
lines.text: The gumbo never has to be done, baby. Isn't that nice? Nothing ever has to be done.
lines.script: [light Louisiana Creole accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] The gumbo never has to be done, baby. Isn't that nice? [light Louisiana Creole accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] Nothing ever has to be done.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: The pupusas are fine. Everything is fine. It's always this afternoon. Why did I ever flip them?
lines.script: [light Salvadoran accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] The pupusas are fine. Everything is fine. [light Salvadoran accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] It's always this afternoon. Why did I ever flip them?

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: The pupusas are fine. Everything is fine.
lines.script: [light Salvadoran accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] The pupusas are fine. Everything is fine.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: It's always this afternoon. Why'd I ever flip them?
lines.script: [light Salvadoran accent, dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] It's always this afternoon. Why'd I ever flip them?

lines.speaker: Marisol
lines.text: I'm walking my dog. I've always been walking my dog.
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] I'm walking my dog. I've always been walking my dog.

lines.speaker: Marisol
lines.text: I'll always be walking my dog. Isn't that nice?
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] I'll always be walking my dog. Isn't that nice?

lines.speaker: Larry
lines.text: I'm blowing leaves. The same leaf. Over and over.
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] I'm blowing leaves. The same leaf. Over and over.

lines.speaker: Larry
lines.text: It never lands. It never has to. Very peaceful.
lines.script: [dazed, dreamy, faraway sing-song monotone] It never lands. It never has to. Very peaceful.
